objective: Replace the unnecessarily strong universal-checker-coverage prerequisite with the exact additive partial-credit mass condition implemented by the pinned LiveBench instruction-following scorer.

per_case_variables.k: number of registered instructions on the case, k >= 1
per_case_variables.s: number of those instructions whose exact check_following predicate returns true, 0 <= s <= k

exact_scorer_algebra.consequence: Every independently proved followed instruction contributes positive score mass even when another instruction on the same case fails; full-case closure contributes an additional 1/2 bonus beyond the instruction-fraction half.

theorem.claim: For the pinned scorer, proving every active instruction type and every allowed conjunction is sufficient but not necessary for LIVEBENCH_IF_GE_65_7. Any precommitted successor whose exact blind benchmark score mass is at least 131.4 closes the predicate, including successors that intentionally leave some instruction predicates unsolved.
proof: The pinned score_results computes score_1 = 1 iff all instructions are followed.
Therefore cases with 0 < s < k receive nonzero score s/(2k).
The benchmark predicate is an aggregate threshold, so acceptance depends on total score mass, not universal checker coverage.

root1_repair_effect.why_stronger: It is logically equivalent to the actual acceptance scorer and strictly weakens unnecessary proof obligations without weakening the target threshold.
